## [0.4.0](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/compare/v0.3.1...v0.4.0) (2026-06-11)

This release turns OpenTaint from a static-analysis CLI into the engine behind an end-to-end, AI-driven application-security workflow — plus a faster install path, new tooling for authoring and testing rules, and clearer scan diagnostics.

## ✨ Highlights

### AI agent skills for application security
OpenTaint now ships a suite of **agent skills** that orchestrate a complete project assessment on top of the analyzer. Add them to your agent with:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/seqra/opentaint
```

The headline `appsec-agent` skill runs the full loop: build the project, run OpenTaint, discover the attack surface, add targeted rules, model missing library data flows, triage findings, and optionally generate dynamic proof-of-concept checks for confirmed vulnerabilities.

The included skills break that loop into composable steps:

- **Scan & triage:** `build-project`, `run-scan`, `analyze-findings`, `generate-poc`
- **Coverage expansion:** `triage-dependencies`, `discover-attack-surface`, `create-test-project`, `create-rule`, `assemble-lib-rules`
- **Dataflow modeling:** `analyze-external-methods`, `create-pass-through-approximation`, `create-dataflow-approximation`, `debug-rule`, `report-analyzer-issue`

### Install via npm / npx
No more platform-specific installers required — OpenTaint is now on npm:

```bash
# Install globally
npm install -g @seqra/opentaint

# Or run instantly, no install (needs Node.js)
npx @seqra/opentaint scan
```

## 🚀 New CLI commands

- **`opentaint test`** — A new command group for authoring and validating detection rules and dataflow approximations. Includes `test rule` (create, run, and debug detection-rule tests, with rule-reachability debugging) and `test approximation` (create and run dataflow-approximation tests). Tests use clear, scriptable exit codes (e.g. `2` for failures, `254` for timeout, `253` for OOM) so they slot cleanly into CI.
- **`opentaint health`** — Shows the resolved on-disk paths and versions for the autobuilder, analyzer, built-in rules, and Java runtime. Select a single component with `--autobuilder`, `--analyzer`, `--rules`, or `--runtime`; exits non-zero when a selected component is missing.

## 🛠️ Improvements

- **Clearer scan diagnostics.** The scan info panel now reports resolved analyzer, autobuilder, and ruleset versions, and labels custom/overridden artifacts as `custom (<path>)` instead of showing an empty version.
- **Relative-lib rules loading.** Library rules referenced by relative paths now resolve correctly during scans and compilation.
- **Better analyzer config handling.** More robust config resolution and project-copy handling in the core analyzer.
- **Updated bundled dependencies.** Refreshed analyzer and autobuilder artifacts (`2026.06.11`) and dependency versions.

## 🧹 Under the hood

- Extracted common, language-agnostic parts of the analyzer (alias analysis, dataflow, taint precondition handling) into a shared core, paving the way for broader language coverage.

## [0.3.0](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/compare/v0.2.1...v0.3.0) (2026-05-15)


A precision-and-robustness release. Lambdas and functional-style Java code
get more accurate taint tracking; rules can now constrain on generic type
arguments and wildcards; alias analysis is more precise and no longer hangs
on a handful of real-world inputs; scans recover cleanly under tight memory
or time limits. The Java XSS ruleset is split into a content-type-aware
ERROR rule and a broader NOTE rule, so CI gates can be wired to ERROR
without drowning in noise.

### Better taint tracking through lambdas

Taint flowing through lambdas and method references is now tracked
flow-sensitively. Only the lambda implementations whose allocation actually
reaches a call site are analyzed there — no more dispatching to every
lambda the analyzer has ever seen for a given functional interface. Traces
through functional-style code are shorter and more precise.

### Generics in rule patterns

Type arguments in your YAML signatures are now actually enforced:

- Patterns like `ResponseEntity<Resource>`, `List<String>`,
  `Map<String, ?>` constrain the match — they used to be silently dropped.
- The `?` wildcard is now first-class in Java patterns.
- A method-decl pattern's return type is checked, so combinations like
  `pattern-inside ResponseEntity<?> $M(...)` with
  `pattern-not-inside ResponseEntity<Integer> $M(...)` filter by return
  type as written.
- Raw uses (`ResponseEntity`) and unbound wildcards (`<?>`) at call sites
  match any pattern's type-argument slot, since they represent unknown
  types.
- Pass-through rules over generic returns (e.g. `List.get` returning `E`)
  continue to match when their pattern is written against the erased type.

When classpath info isn't available to resolve the generic view of a
method, matching falls back to erased-name semantics rather than going
silent.

### Alias analysis: precision and reliability

- Heap-only alias relations are no longer thrown away. When two fields or
  array elements are known to alias but no local variable in the current
  method holds either, the analyzer now keeps that relation and uses it
  for taint propagation.
- An unsound strong update on array stores has been removed. Writing
  `arr[i] = …` no longer kills aliasing on the rest of the array.
- The algorithm that invalidates aliases reachable from method-outer
  locations has been rewritten. Two real-world inputs that previously hung
  the analyzer or produced bursts of false positives are now stable.
- Long alias-resolution chains now respond to cancel signals immediately
  instead of running to completion.

### Robustness under tight memory and time limits

- Cancel signals (timeout, memory pressure) now propagate into the inner
  loops of the analyzer. Previously a global cancel could be ignored while
  the alias or summary fixed point was still running; now it takes effect
  promptly.
- The source-file indexer no longer re-indexes the same source root once
  per registered project location. Projects with many locations sharing
  source roots use less memory and CPU at startup.
- Class-name extraction no longer swallows `OutOfMemoryError` or
  `StackOverflowError`. Under memory pressure the scan now fails with a
  clear error instead of continuing with corrupted intermediate state.

### Autobuilder skips hidden directories

The Gradle and Maven autobuilders now skip any directory whose name starts
with `.` under the project root (`.git`, `.idea`, `.gradle`, `.opentaint`,
vendored build caches, …). Previously they could descend into these and
sometimes pick up build outputs as real source projects.

### Bundled rule additions

Spring `DeferredResult` is now a recognized pass-through, so taint flows
through `setResult` / `setErrorResult` in Spring async endpoints.

### Java XSS: ERROR and NOTE tiers

The single XSS rule for Servlet and Spring is now a pair per framework:

- **ERROR-tier** — `xss-in-servlet-app`, `xss-in-spring-app`. Fires only
  when the response content type is statically confirmed to be `text/html`:
  an explicit `setContentType("text/html…")`, `produces = "text/html"` on a
  Spring mapping, or a response builder with `contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)`.
  Suitable for blocking CI gates.
- **NOTE-tier** — `response-injection-in-servlet-app`,
  `response-injection-in-spring-app`. Fires on any direct write of
  untrusted input into a response writer or Spring response, regardless of
  content type. Catches the broader pattern at lower confidence.

Both tiers share the same sanitizer list: OWASP Java Encoder
(`Encode.forHtml`), OWASP HTML Sanitizer (`PolicyFactory.sanitize`),
AntiSamy (`scan`), JSoup (`clean`), Spring `HtmlUtils.htmlEscape`, Apache
Commons `StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml{,3,4}`, and OWASP ESAPI
`encodeForHTML`. For Spring, `ResponseEntity` constructions whose headers
were set to a non-HTML content type are also treated as sanitized.

ERROR rules ship with full CWE-79 documentation: vulnerable example, two
safe examples (HTML encoding and DTO-returning), references, and
provenance.

### CLI

The "update available" check no longer runs during the `update` command
itself. The running process is on the *old* version, so the check would
otherwise queue a stale "update available" hint for the version that's
currently being installed.

### Install / upgrade

*fresh install*
```
curl -fsSL https://opentaint.org/install.sh | bash
```
```
irm https://opentaint.org/install.ps1 | iex
```
```
brew install --cask seqra/tap/opentaint
```

*in-place upgrade*
```
opentaint self-update
```

* **analyzer:** Enhance type-aware pattern matching and generic type handling ([#99](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/issues/99)) ([c19a8bc](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/commit/c19a8bc88c4bae9e314b9d58d816e798ce185433))

## [0.2.0](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0) (2026-04-17)

A quality-of-life release: scans run with no flags, compiled project models are cached and shared safely
between processes, and the analysis engine got a substantial IFDS rework.

### Scan: zero-friction defaults

- opentaint scan now defaults to the current directory — no path argument required.
- `-o`/`--output` is no longer mandatory; SARIF is written to a default location.
- New `--project-model <path>`: scan a pre-compiled project model and skip compilation.
- New `--recompile`: force a fresh build even when a cached model exists.
- New `--log-file <path>`: redirect logs explicitly.

### Compilation model cache

- Compiled project models are cached under `~/.opentaint/`. Repeated scans of the same project skip compilation
unless `--recompile` is passed.

### Safe concurrency

- New reader/writer lock API protects the model cache, prune operations, and install state.
- Concurrent scan, prune, and self-update invocations do not corrupt shared state — conflicting operations
either wait or fail loudly with a clear message.

### prune reworked

- Selective category flags: `--artifacts`, `--rules`, `--jdk`, `--models`, `--logs`, `--install`.
- `--all` for a full sweep including install-tier and logs.
- Default (no flags): artifacts + rules + jdk + models.
- Active compilations are surfaced as "Skipped" instead of silently touched.
- Auto-prune removed from self-update; users are nudged to run opentaint prune explicitly.

### `--debug` replaces `--verbosity`

- Single boolean `-d`/`--debug` flag replaces the old --verbosity string.
- Streams JAR subprocess output and reveals debug-only fields.
- GitHub Action mirrors this: the verbosity input is now a boolean debug input (#97).

### Analysis engine

- Major rework of the IFDS access-tree representation, access-graph, summary storage, and analysis runner —
better scalability on large Spring applications.
- pass-rules handling reworked for correctness.

### Install / upgrade

*fresh install*
`curl -sSL https://opentaint.org/install.sh | sh`

*in-place upgrade*
`opentaint self-update`

* **cli:** Add scan defaults and compilation model caching ([#89](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/issues/89)) ([bc65934](https://github.com/seqra/opentaint/commit/bc65934bb502284562c43fe1eb9e28a1eec61db3))
